To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel semantically guided generative model for inpainting of video sequences.
(i) our model can inpaint a video sequence of arbitrary length, (ii) it can generate consistent inpaintings across the sequence, and (iii) it can preserve the facial expressions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental problem of learning a consistent generative model for inpainting.

the following contributions: (1) We present a semantically guided GAN for inpainting which is capable of producing highly consistent and correct results; (2) We demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms the current state-of-the art methods in terms of quantitative and qualitative evaluation; (3) We provide a comprehensive analysis of the proposed approach and demonstrate its effectiveness on different datasets, deformations and resolutions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to leverage the underlying semantics in the data to improve the consistency of generative models.
we present a sematically guided Generative Adversial Network (GAN) that learns to inpaint a face sequence by simultaneously improving consistency and correctness of the reconstructions.
we are the first to propose a generative model for video inpainting which can be used for both consistency and correctness of inpainted videos.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed model can be easily extended to other domains such as videos and 3D scenes, and can be applied for other tasks, such as image completion.
the consistency and correctness can be achieved by leveraging the semantic information in the generative process.
the proposed semantically guided GAN formulation can be used as a general purpose framework to improve inpainting performance of any generative model.
